scope: Packed retained Lynx SDK arm64 Release executions on iOS Simulator and Android emulator. Both the native acceptance subclass and unmodified generated default startup/layout execute the public retained TauriView component. The exact original WebView moves between parents; its nonpersistent document token and native navigation/UI delegates or clients remain unchanged. Actual frontend geolocation/save and capability denial share Tauri state with direct native calls. Simultaneous second attachment is rejected without stealing the first view. Component unmount/remount, renderer replacement and close restore the original view and retain the document. Native renderer sessions are retired independently of the original Tauri document.

iosContextFailure.scope: First implementation read Lynx UI context during createView, before Lynx assigns it; real UI reported view_unavailable. Final code resolves the generation scope at attachment.

numericFlexDiagnostic.scope: Native attachment preserved the document, but fixture numeric flex produced zero height in pinned Lynx. Instrumented same-SDK Release diagnosis measured 369x0 before and 369x350 after CSS string flex; the latter delivered real embedded Tauri capability denial. These diagnostic consumers were manually instrumented, not final generated acceptance.

timestampAssertion.scope: Actual embedded frontend save/native session parity passed. Exact performance.timeOrigin equality then failed with values differing by about 2 ms. Final acceptance tracks an immutable nonpersistent per-document token installed only by native test instrumentation at composition startup; a reload or replacement loses it. Time origin remains diagnostic data, not the document identity assertion.
